page.layout: One printed page (left, verso-style page 78) with a single text column; at its right edge a narrow strip of margin notes from the facing page, cut off and partly unreadable. The notes strip belongs to the right side of the scan and is shown as a fragment of the adjacent page.

main_text.p: tante, tum sequentibus diebus sen-tiente, & ita deinceps; probabilita-te caret. Membra enim humana non inserviunt animæ quæ tantum est ve-getans, aut sentiens; sed rationali, quæ virtualiter superiores duas in se continet. Fœtus ergo animatus in utero nutritur, & crescit quousque robur acquirat, & ore nutriri possit, indigeatque non tantum majore loco, sed & liberaliore cordis refrigerio. Tum, duce naturâ, calcitrando membranas & involucra rumpit. Confpirat tamen uterus, sefeq; pandit: nec hic solum, sed & vicinæ partes.

In partu naturali & legitimo infans caput & humeros primò exerit; quo facto, reliquæ partes non difficulter sequuntur: si enim brachium, pes aut alia pars in lucem primò prodeat, partus non carebit periculo.
Tempora partus humani incerta sunt. Constat tamen ante sextum mensem, non esse fœtum vitalem. Septimo quidem mense est vitalis, & quod

page.notes: The right-hand strip is the cropped margin/running text of the facing page (fragments such as "Institut", "& quod", "Natur", "Sed", "& Me") and is not transcribed beyond these fragments. The first line of the printed page reads "78 GILBERTI IACCHÆI" with the page number at left. The final word "quod" is printed right-aligned at the foot of the text block. Some letters in the scan are soft and were read with reasonable confidence; no [?] markers were needed for the main text.
